gates.evidence: 4 amended versions detected in the last 30 days
gates.unmeasured_reason: No RA amendment ledger for this cell. The denominator is what the authority actually published, which only after-the-fact manual comparison can supply — the system's own count of what it saw would score 100% by construction. Author docs/eval/ground_truth/amendment_ledger.json to measure this.
caveats: Poll completion 76.2%: 493 of 647 scheduled polls ran over 30 days across 85 sources (154 missed). Detection coverage measured over observed polls would have divided by the polls that happened rather than the polls that were due, and downtime would have improved it.

gates.evidence: 4 alert(s) in the window, none of them measurable: 4 backfill, 0 with no publication date
gates.unmeasured_reason: No alert in the window covers an amendment published while this cell was under observation, so there is nothing the gate can be measured on yet. Latency from our own retrieval clock — worst case 123.731h — bounds our pipeline, not the gate. This resolves itself: the first amendment published after ingestion started is measurable.
caveats: 4 alert(s) cover amendments published before this cell came under observation (2026-08-03T06:47:00.137638+00:00) and are excluded: publication → alert on a backfilled corpus measures how long the instrument existed before RegOps arrived, not how fast RegOps noticed.
